title: Hash tables
summary: O(1) lookups: turn a key into a bucket number.

cards.title: Lockers with a formula
cards.body:
If the locker number could be **computed** from the key, you'd go straight to it. A **hash function** does that: key → number → bucket.

Different keys can land in the same bucket (a **collision**). Chaining keeps a short list per bucket; growing the table keeps the lists short.
Watch the rehash step: when the table grows, every key's bucket changes, because `% size` changed.
`std::unordered_map` and `std::unordered_set` work like this. Average O(1); a terrible hash that sends everything to one bucket degrades to O(n).

cards.question: Why does the table grow when keys / buckets > 0.75?
choices: To keep each bucket's list short, so lookups stay O(1) on average
cards.explain: More keys per bucket means longer lists to scan. Growing spreads keys over more buckets.
